citeAs: Jian Xie, Kai Zhang, Jiangjie Chen, Tinghui Zhu, Renze Lou, Yuandong Tian, Yanghua Xiao, Yu Su (2024). TravelPlanner: A Benchmark for Real-World Planning with Language Agents. arXiv:2402.01622.
creator: Jian Xie, Kai Zhang, Jiangjie Chen, Tinghui Zhu, Renze Lou, Yuandong Tian, Yanghua Xiao, Yu Su (Fudan University, The Ohio State University, The Pennsylvania State University, Meta AI)
description: TravelPlanner is a planning benchmark focused on travel planning that provides a rich sandbox environment with around four million data entries crawled from the Internet, accessible via six tools. It includes 1,225 meticulously curated planning intents and reference plans, evaluating whether language agents can develop flexible travel plans by collecting information via diverse tools and making decisions while satisfying multiple constraints (user needs and commonsense constraints).
name: TravelPlanner
publisher: OSU NLP Group (The Ohio State University)
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Quality control was performed by the authors who reviewed every query and plan, rectifying any errors. Budgets were re-calibrated using costs from human-annotated plans. Plans were validated against an automated evaluation script to ensure feasibility. The process resulted in 1,225 validated query-plan pairs.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Twenty graduate students were invited to meticulously annotate plans for synthesized queries. A plan was deemed eligible only if it met all the constraints outlined in the evaluation script. Authors performed a detailed review of every query and plan, rectifying any errors found. Budgets were re-calibrated using costs from corresponding human-annotated plans to replace initial heuristic-generated budgets. Annotators were paid an average of $0.80 per plan.
rai:dataBiases: The benchmark uses a static and closed sandbox environment to avoid variability and potential biases introduced by dynamic data. Data was modified from original sources to avoid data contamination. The authors acknowledge that everyone's definition of commonsense may be different, and current evaluation criteria are based on the authors' consensus.
rai:dataCollection: Data was collected from multiple sources: flight data from the Kaggle Flight Status Prediction dataset (spanning 2022-03-01 to 2022-04-01), driving distance/time from the Google Distance Matrix API, restaurant data from the Kaggle Zomato Restaurants Dataset, attraction data from the Google Places API, and accommodation data from the Kaggle Airbnb Open Data Dataset. The original data was then modified (adding, deleting, and altering certain keys and values) to suit benchmark requirements and avoid data contamination.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data sources include: (1) Kaggle Flight Status Prediction dataset for flight data; (2) Google Distance Matrix API for driving distances and travel times; (3) Kaggle Zomato Restaurants Dataset for restaurant names and average costs; (4) Google Places API for attraction information; (5) Kaggle Airbnb Open Data Dataset for accommodation details.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Web API, Manual Human Curator
rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark uses a static and closed sandbox environment, which may not fully reflect the dynamic nature of real-world travel planning. The commonsense evaluation criteria are based on the authors' consensus, and everyone's definition of commonsense may differ. The dataset strictly prohibits any form of cheating in the validation and test sets.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Original data was modified by adding, deleting, and altering certain keys and values to suit benchmark requirements and avoid data contamination. Restaurants were randomly assigned to cities and randomly categorized under cuisine types. Accommodations were randomly assigned to cities and given random room rules. Flight prices were generated by multiplying distance by a random factor (0.2 to 0.5). Query budgets were re-calibrated using costs from human-annotated plans to replace initial heuristic-generated budgets.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For FlightSearch: extracted fields including FlightDate, DepTime, ArrTime, ActualElapsedTime, Distance, OriginCityName, DestCityName; generated Price by multiplying Distance by a random factor (0.2 to 0.5). For DistanceMatrix: calculated Price for self-driving and taxi by multiplying Distance by factors of 1 and 0.15 respectively. For RestaurantSearch: extracted Restaurant Name and Average Cost, randomly assigned restaurants to cities, randomly categorized each restaurant under cuisine types. For AccommodationSearch: extracted NAME, room type, price, minimum nights, review rate number, maximum occupancy; randomly assigned items to cities and assigned random room rules.
rai:dataSocialImpact: TravelPlanner provides a challenging yet meaningful testbed for future language agents to hill-climb toward human-level planning in complex settings. The benchmark may help automate tedious travel planning tasks for humans. Some data is derived from publicly available Internet data, and the content does not represent the authors' viewpoints. The authors strictly prohibit cheating in validation and test sets to uphold fairness and reliability.
rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating language agents' capabilities in complex multi-constraint planning and tool use; benchmarking LLMs on real-world travel planning tasks; testing agents' ability to use tools to collect information and satisfy diverse constraints; training language agents using reinforcement learning techniques with evaluation feedback from the training set.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4 was used to generate natural language queries from structured JSON elements. GPT-4-Turbo was used to extract key components (transportation, restaurants, attractions, accommodations) from natural language plans for evaluation.

null_reasons.rai:annotationsPerItem: The paper does not specify the number of independent annotations per item; it only states that each query has at least one feasible plan annotated.
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: No specific annotation platform (e.g., MTurk, Label Studio) is mentioned; annotation was done by graduate students directly.
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The paper does not explicitly discuss missing data handling in the collection process.
null_reasons.rai:dataImputationProtocol: No imputation protocol for missing values is described in the paper.
null_reasons.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: No versioning, update cadence, or maintenance plan is described beyond releasing evaluation scripts.
null_reasons.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset contains travel planning data (flights, restaurants, accommodations, attractions) with no personal or sensitive information about individuals.
null_reasons.license: License not stated in the paper; sourced from HuggingFace metadata only, and evidence_quote must come from paper text.
